en.headline: Government proposes HK$10 billion capital injection for San Tin Technopole Company
en.dek: The Innovation and Technology Bureau has submitted a paper to the Legislative Council outlining how the initial funding will be used to accelerate land formation and develop innovation sites.
body: The Government has proposed to create a commitment to inject HK$10 billion from the Capital Investment Fund as share capital into the San Tin Technopole Company, according to a paper submitted by the Innovation, Technology and Industry Bureau to the Legislative Council.

Of the initial funding, about HK$3 billion is reserved for accelerating land formation through diversified development modes that can engage market resources. About HK$6 billion is earmarked for developing innovation and technology sites, including the design and construction of industry facilities for lease to attract enterprises. The remaining about HK$1 billion is for early operating expenses of the company.

The paper states that of the approximately 210 hectares of innovation and technology land at San Tin Technopole, about 140 hectares are expected to be available over the next five years. The company may need to invest in building industry facilities itself in the early stages to attract tenants. It can also explore joint ventures or land-share arrangements with enterprises, institutions and research bodies.

According to the Government’s preliminary estimates, when fully operational the Technopole is expected to contribute about HK$200 billion or more to Hong Kong’s GDP annually and provide about 200,000 full-time jobs.

zh.headline: 政府建議向新田科技城公司注資100億元作為起始資金
zh.dek: 創新科技及工業局向立法會提交文件，建議從資本投資基金撥出100億元予新田科技城公司，當中60億元發展創科用地、30億元加快土地平整。
body: 創新科技及工業局向立法會提交文件，建議開立一筆承擔額，以便從資本投資基金撥出100億元，作為給予新田科技城公司的注資股本。
起始資金中，約30億元預留以多元發展模式加快土地平整，善用市場力量；約60億元用以發展創科用地，包括由公司設計和建造產業設施作出租，以吸引企業落戶；餘下約10億元支付公司早期營運開支。
文件指出，新田科技城約210公頃創新科技用地中，政府預計未來5年約140公頃土地產出。公司起步階段或須自行投入資金興建產業設施，亦可考慮以股份制或土地參股等方式與企業合組公司共同開發。
據政府初步估算，新田科技城完全運作後，預計每年可為本地生產總值帶來約2,000億元或以上貢獻，並提供約20萬個相關全職職位。
